verdicts.rationale: The proposal establishes that edge reconciliation (upsert + delete) runs inside the per-entry atomic transaction; the candidate builds on exactly that foundation by specifying what structured payload that transaction returns so downstream renderers know which scopes were affected by those edge writes. The two decisions are complementary layers of the same commit pipeline — one defines what happens to edges, the other defines what the transaction reports about the consequences. No commitment in either reverses the other.

The proposal governs when and how outgoing edges are reconciled (upsert/delete inside the atomic transaction); the candidate governs how slug citations are resolved to node IDs before those edges are written. These are sequential steps in the same pipeline and neither reverses the other — a coherent architecture can apply case-insensitive lookup during resolution and then declaratively reconcile the resulting edges.

The proposal concerns edge-table reconciliation semantics (upsert declared edges, delete undeclared ones) inside the per-entry transaction; the candidate concerns write semantics for the separate `signals` table within that same transaction. They govern distinct tables and distinct concerns, and both can be honoured simultaneously inside one atomic transaction without any contradiction.

The proposal is entirely about edge-graph reconciliation logic; the candidate is entirely about parser tokenisation rules for HTML comments. They operate at different layers of the pipeline (parsing vs. graph writes) and share no load-bearing commitments that could conflict.

The proposal governs the SQLite-side edge reconciliation within commit transactions; the candidate governs how Qdrant vector collections are namespaced per project. These address entirely separate subsystems (graph store vs. vector store) with no overlapping commitments, and a single architecture can honour both without tension.
